name: Neptune (IP65 low glare)
faq:
Q: What is the Neptune downlight and when is it typically specified?
A: Neptune is a low glare IP65 downlight built as a direct replacement for older PL lamp fittings, giving contractors a straightforward LED upgrade path on refurbishment work. Its IP65 rating and IK05 impact resistance suit bathrooms, kitchens, and washrooms as well as standard commercial ceilings. It spans four cutout sizes from 100mm to 200mm and wattages from 8W to 32W, so one range covers several room types on a single project.

Q: What reflector finish options does Neptune offer?
A: Neptune uses magnetic reflectors available in polished chrome, white, matte silver, or titanium, letting specifiers match the fitting to different interior finishes without changing the base unit. Because the reflectors are magnetic, they can be swapped or serviced without disturbing the housing. This gives designers flexibility to align the visual finish with door furniture or other metalwork in a scheme.

Q: What sizes and wattages does Neptune come in?
A: Neptune's wattage is tied to cutout size: the 100mm cutout runs at 8W or 16W, the 150mm cutout at 12W or 22W, the 170mm cutout at 13W or 26W, and the 200mm cutout at 16W or 32W. This spread lets a single product family cover smaller circulation areas through to larger open plan spaces on the same job. Both 3000K and 4000K colour temperatures are available across the range.

Q: What performance and lifetime figures does Neptune offer?
A: Neptune delivers an efficacy of around 106 lm/W with a CRI above 90 Ra, giving good colour rendering alongside energy efficient output. It carries an L70 B50 rating of 100,000 hours and an SDCM of 3 or less, meaning colour consistency stays tight across a batch of fittings. It is backed by a 5 year warranty as standard.

Q: Can Neptune be dimmed or specified for emergency circuits?
A: Neptune can be specified with DALI, 0-10V, or DSI dimming, or with Casambi wireless control, so it can integrate with most standard commercial lighting control systems. An emergency pack and a DALI addressable emergency pack are also available as accessories, along with a Z10 remote control emergency kit. This means the same retrofit downlight can serve both standard and emergency lighting circuits.

Q: How does Neptune compare to other PL replacement downlights in the range?
A: Neptune and Carina are both designed as replacements for older PL lamp downlights, but they differ in protection level and finish choice. Neptune carries an IP65 rating and a choice of four magnetic reflector finishes, making it suited to areas needing moisture resistance and a coordinated metal finish. Carina is rated IP20 and focuses more on dimming and emergency lighting options, so the choice often comes down to whether wet area protection or reflector finish matters more for a given room.

Q: What should specifiers check before ordering Neptune for a retrofit?
A: Because Neptune's wattage options are tied to each specific cutout size, for example the 100mm cutout is available in 8W or 16W while the 200mm cutout runs to 16W or 32W, specifiers should match the existing ceiling aperture to the correct cutout and wattage combination before ordering. This keeps the retrofit straightforward and avoids cutting new holes in an existing ceiling. Checking the reflector finish and dimming requirements at the same time avoids a second order later.

name: E-Pro (architectural downlight)
faq:
Q: What is the E-Pro range designed for?
A: E-Pro is a range of linear and square cellular downlights for architectural interiors where a discreet and low glare fitting matters. The E-pro fitting can be used to achieve UGR below 19. It suits office ceilings, reception areas, and other spaces where visual comfort around screens is a specification priority. The range is available in a wide choice of cell configurations, so one product family can be used consistently across different room shapes.

Q: What cell configurations and mounting options does E-Pro offer?
A: The recessed E-Pro range is available in single cell, 1x3, 1x5, 1x10, 2x2, and 3x3 cell configurations, while the surface mounted version is offered in single cell, 2x2, and 3x3 formats. This gives specifiers layouts from small individual fittings to long linear runs, and lets ceiling void depth or structure guide the choice between recessed and surface mounting. Finishes are available in black RAL9005 or matte white RAL9016 to suit the surrounding ceiling.

Q: What makes E-Pro's optics different from a standard downlight?
A: E-Pro uses purpose designed optics to hold glare below a UGR of 19 for the fitting, which is relevant in spaces such as offices with screen based work where visual comfort is a specification priority. This low glare performance is combined with the flexibility of multiple cell layouts rather than being limited to one fixed format. The result is a consistent, discreet appearance across an architectural ceiling scheme.

Q: What dimming and colour temperature options are available with E-Pro?
A: E-Pro can be specified with DALI, 0-10V, or DSI dimming, or with Casambi wireless control, so it can integrate with standard commercial lighting control systems. Colour temperature options are 3000K or 4000K, giving flexibility to match warmer or cooler commercial environments. Wattage varies by cell configuration, from a single cell option up to the largest multi-cell formats.

Q: What are the technical performance figures for E-Pro?
A: E-Pro delivers an efficacy of around 100 to 106 lm/W with a CRI above 90 Ra and a 50 degree beam angle, giving strong colour rendering suited to design led interiors. It is rated IP40 with an IK07 impact rating, a 100,000 hour L70 B50 lifetime, and a 5 year warranty. These figures support specification in standard indoor commercial environments.

name: Core
faq:
Q: Is the Core downlight firerated?
A: Yes, Core is a fire rated downlight tested at 30, 60, and 90 minute ratings, including testing with I-joist ceiling constructions, which matters for compliance on projects using engineered timber joists. This makes it a relevant choice where building regulations require ceiling fire integrity to be maintained around recessed fittings. Its IP65 front also allows use in areas where moisture resistance is needed.

Q: Can Core's colour temperature be changed after installation?
A: Core has a switchable colour temperature between 3000K and 4000K, adjusted using a dip switch located behind the bezel. This means the same stocked fitting can be set to warm white or cool white on site depending on the scheme. It removes the need to fix colour temperature at order stage if requirements change later.

Q: What bezel options are available for Core?
A: Core is supplied with an integrated dimmable driver and offers interchangeable bezels as an option, including chrome, metal brushed chrome, and black finishes on top of the standard white and black bodies. This lets a contractor fit a standard bezel initially and swap to a different finish to suit the final interior design without replacing the whole downlight. It gives flexibility to adjust the visual finish after first fix.

Q: What are the light output and performance figures for Core?
A: Core delivers 602 lumens from a 6W fitting with a CRI above 80 Ra and a 60 degree beam angle, giving a reasonable balance of colour rendering and output for fire rated ceilings. It has an L70 B50 rated lifetime of 50,000 hours and is backed by a 5 year warranty. The integrated dimmable driver means dimming control is built in rather than needing a separate driver specified.

Q: Where is the Core downlight suitable for installation?
A: Core's IP65 front rating and fire rated ceiling performance make it suitable for spaces requiring both moisture resistance and fire compliance, such as bathrooms or corridors in multi-occupancy buildings. Because it has been tested with I-joist ceilings, it is a practical specification for new build or refurbishment projects using engineered floor and ceiling systems. The switchable colour temperature and bezel options add flexibility for the final fit-out.

name: R3
faq:
Q: What does "all-in-one" mean for the R3 downlight?
A: R3 is described as an all-in-one fire rated IP65 downlight, combining fire protection, water resistance, and tunable colour temperature control in a single fitting rather than requiring separate accessories to achieve each feature. This simplifies specification and ordering for contractors who need one product to satisfy multiple performance requirements. It is available in tunable or fixed colour temperature versions depending on project needs.

Q: How is colour temperature adjusted on the R3 downlight?
A: R3 can be tuned from 3000K through to 5000K. A wall switch cycles through the settings in quick succession, moving from 3000K to 4000K to a dimmed night mode and on to 5000K, while a remote control smoothly dims from 100% down to 10% and adjusts colour temperature across the same range. This gives on-site flexibility to adjust the light to suit the time of day without rewiring or replacing fittings.

Q: What bezel finishes are available for R3?
A: R3 offers a choice of four different bezels: white as standard, plus chrome, brushed chrome, and black options. This allows the same downlight platform to be finished to suit a range of different interior styles without changing the underlying fitting. It gives specifiers flexibility to match other metal finishes in a scheme.

Q: What is the light output and rated lifetime of R3?
A: R3 produces 591 lumens from a 6W fitting with a CRI above 90 Ra and a 55 degree beam angle. It carries an L70 B50 rated lifetime of 70,000 hours and is backed by a 5 year warranty, giving specifiers a documented basis for lifetime and colour performance expectations. Its IP65 rating supports use in areas where moisture resistance is required alongside fire performance.

Q: Can multiple R3 downlights be controlled together?
A: R3 shares a remote control with the Centorio range that can operate up to 100 downlights per channel across 4 individually switched rooms or circuits, up to 400 downlights in total. This is useful on projects with multiple rooms needing consistent colour temperature and dimming control without a full building management system. It suits fit-outs where simple, centralised control of several fittings is required.

Q: How does R3 compare to Core within the range?
A: R3 and Core are both fire rated IP65 all-in-one downlights, but R3 offers continuous colour tuning from 3000K to 5000K with a 55 degree beam angle, a CRI above 90 Ra, and a 70,000 hour L70 B50 lifetime. Core is limited to a fixed switch between 3000K and 4000K, with a CRI above 80 Ra and a 50,000 hour L70 B50 lifetime. R3 also shares a remote control with Centorio for managing multiple downlights across several rooms.

name: Pinnacle
faq:
Q: What is the Pinnacle spotlight best suited for?
A: Pinnacle is a fixed mini spot light designed for prestigious applications, where a focused, decorative beam is wanted rather than general area lighting. It is available with a white or titanium reflector, making it suitable for high end retail, hospitality, or feature lighting schemes. The compact fixed spot format suits accenting artwork, displays, or architectural features.

Q: What beam angle options does Pinnacle offer?
A: Pinnacle comes with a standard 15 degree beam angle for tight, focused spot lighting, with optional 38 degree or 55 degree beam angles available where a wider spread is needed. This lets one product range cover both tight accent lighting and broader wash effects depending on the beam angle selected at order stage. The beam angle choice allows the fitting to be matched to the specific object or area being highlighted.

Q: What dimming options are available with Pinnacle?
A: Pinnacle can be specified with mains dimming, DALI, 0-10V, or DSI dimming, or with Casambi wireless control, allowing it to integrate with standard commercial lighting control systems used elsewhere on a project. It is supplied in a single 3000K colour temperature. This flexibility allows the fitting to be matched to existing control infrastructure rather than needing a bespoke solution.

Q: What performance and warranty does Pinnacle carry?
A: Pinnacle delivers an efficacy of around 99 lm/W with a CRI above 90 Ra, giving good colour rendering for feature and accent lighting applications. It has an L70 B50 rated lifetime of 100,000 hours and is backed by a 5 year warranty. It is rated IP20, so it is intended for standard indoor use rather than damp or exterior locations.

Q: What reflector finish options does Pinnacle offer?
A: Pinnacle is available with a white or a titanium reflector, giving a choice between a clean, understated look and a more discreet contemporary decorative touch. This makes Pinnacle suitable for hospitality and retail settings wanting to coordinate the fitting's appearance with the rest of the scheme. The reflector choice is independent of the beam angle selected.

name: Endor (customisable)
faq:
Q: What is the concept behind the Endor downlight range?
A: Endor was designed to let specifiers create diverse lighting environments using one luminaire range, so a project can maintain a consistent style even where different applications and finishes are needed. Designers can combine different wattages, beam angles, housings, and reflector finishes within the same family, using CREE COB LED modules and Tridonic drivers. This makes it a practical choice where a scheme spans multiple room types but needs visual consistency.

Q: What housing and reflector choices does Endor offer?
A: Endor is available in round, round rimless, or square housing design options, with reflector finishes in titanium, matte silver, or polished chrome across both the downlight and wallwasher versions. Beam angles can be specified at 15, 38, or 55 degrees depending on the desired lighting effect. All four wattage tiers share the same choice of finishes and beam angles.

Q: Does Endor offer wet area protection as well as standard indoor versions?
A: Endor is available in a standard IP20 housing for indoor use, with a special IP65 housing offered for the 12W size across all three beam angle options. This means the same customisable reflector and beam angle choices can be extended into a wet area such as a bathroom without switching to a visually different product. It supports keeping one consistent luminaire family across a building where some rooms need extra moisture resistance.

Q: Is Endor available as a wallwasher as well as a downlight?
A: Endor's product codes cover both a downlight version and a wallwasher version at every wattage tier, beam angle, and reflector finish combination. This means the same range can deliver straight-down illumination in one part of a room and directional wall lighting in another, using matching finishes throughout. It keeps the visual language of a scheme consistent even where the lighting task changes from room to room.

Q: How do you specify the exact Endor configuration you need?
A: Endor uses a modular part code system where the wattage tier, beam angle, housing, and reflector finish are each selected as separate code elements and combined into one part number, for example R0966A1B1C1E1/3K for a 12W downlight with a 15 degree beam, titanium reflector, in 3000K. This lets a specifier build a precise combination from a shared set of building blocks rather than choosing from a fixed list of pre-set models. Or lighting design team can select the best Engor configurations for your space.

name: Sirius (commercial)
faq:
Q: What is the Sirius downlight designed for?
A: Sirius is a recessed high output downlight with a 210mm cutout, designed for commercial applications where higher light output is needed from a single fitting. It is available in a standard 24W version or a high output 42W version, delivering up to 4418 lumens, which suits larger open areas such as offices, retail floors, or commercial circulation spaces. Its CRI above 90 Ra ensures good colour rendering for these environments.

Q: Should I specify the 24W or 42W version of Sirius?
A: Sirius is available in 24W, producing 2511 to 2525 lumens, or 42W, producing 4401 to 4418 lumens, with a choice of 3000K or 4000K colour temperature either way. Larger commercial spaces or areas with higher ceilings generally benefit from the 42W version to maintain adequate light levels, while 24W may be sufficient for smaller rooms. Checking the required lux level for the space is the best way to decide between the two. Our lighting design team can offer this as a complementary service.

Q: What is the rated performance and lifetime of Sirius?
A: Sirius delivers an efficacy of around 105 lm/W with a 40 degree beam angle and an L70 B50 rated lifetime of 100,000 hours. It carries a 5 year warranty and an SDCM of 3 or less, supporting consistent colour output across multiple fittings on a large installation. It is rated IP20, suiting standard indoor commercial ceilings.

Q: What finish options are available for Sirius?
A: Sirius is available with either a white or black bezel finish, allowing it to be matched to the ceiling colour or design scheme of the space. This is useful in commercial fit-outs where the bezel finish needs to coordinate with other ceiling-mounted equipment. The finish choice is independent of the wattage and colour temperature options, giving flexibility when specifying.

Q: What if my existing cutout doesn't match Sirius's 210mm size?
A: A cutout extension ring accessory is available for Sirius, adjusting the aperture up to around 250 to 270mm where an existing ceiling hole is larger than the standard 210mm cutout. This is a practical option on refurbishment projects replacing an older, larger fitting. Please always check the existing cutout on site before ordering.

name: Ultra Slim
faq:
Q: What is the Ultra Slim downlight designed for?
A: Ultra Slim is a round downlight designed for low ceiling voids, with a profile of less than 30mm deep across all five sizes, making it ideal where there is limited space above the ceiling. It offers a clean finish suited to any environment, from residential refurbishments to commercial fit-outs with restricted void depth. This slim profile is a key differentiator from standard recessed downlights that require deeper ceiling voids.

Q: Is Ultra Slim suitable for damp areas?
A: Ultra Slim carries an IP54 rating with an IK09 impact rating, giving it protection against dust and splashing water that is higher than many standard indoor downlights. This makes it a reasonable option for areas such as kitchens or utility spaces where some moisture exposure is expected, in addition to standard dry commercial ceilings. A TP(a) rated diffuser is also available as an upgrade from the standard TP(b) rated diffuser.

Q: Can Ultra Slim be used with emergency lighting or dimming?
A: Ultra Slim is available in dimmable or non-dimming standard versions, plus an emergency lighting option, giving specifiers flexibility to match the fitting to the electrical requirements of a particular room. This means the same slim-profile design can be used consistently across a project even where some rooms require emergency provision and others do not. The dimming and emergency options are selected alongside the wattage and colour temperature at order stage.

Q: What beam angle does Ultra Slim use and what does that mean for coverage?
A: Ultra Slim has a wide 90 degree beam angle, which spreads light broadly from a single fitting and helps deliver even coverage in shallow ceiling voids where multiple narrower-beam downlights might otherwise be needed. This wide spread, combined with its clean, near-flush finish, suits open-plan rooms wanting soft, general illumination rather than defined pools of light. It works alongside the five available wattage and size options to match coverage to room size.

Q: What if my existing cutout doesn't match one of Ultra Slim's standard sizes?
A: An extension ring accessory is available for the 23W Ultra Slim to adjust its cutout size, which is useful on refurbishment projects where an existing hole in the ceiling does not exactly match one of the five standard cutout options. This avoids the need to cut a new, larger hole and helps keep plasterwork repairs to a minimum. It is worth checking cutout dimensions on site against the product range before ordering.

name: Carina
faq:
Q: Can the Carina downlight replace older PL lamp downlights?
A: Yes. Carina is designed as a cost and energy efficient replacement for older PL lamp downlights, giving contractors an LED upgrade path for existing compact fluorescent fittings. It is designed to reduce glare compared with older lamp technology while delivering good thermal control. This makes it a practical retrofit option for wholesalers supplying replacement stock for refurbishment work.

Q: What size and wattage range does Carina cover?
A: Carina is available in four sizes with wattages of 12W, 15W, 18W, or 23W, and in two colour temperatures, 3000K or 4000K. This range allows one product family to suit a variety of room sizes and applications on the same project. An extension ring accessory is available for the largest 23W cutout size.

Q: Does Carina support dimming or emergency lighting?
A: Carina can be specified with dimming options, including mains, DALI, 0-10V, or DSI dimming, as well as an emergency lighting version. This gives specifiers the flexibility to use the same downlight family in both standard and emergency circuits, or where lighting control is required. These options are selected at order stage alongside size and colour temperature.

Q: How does Carina manage heat and glare?
A: Carina is built to deliver good thermal control alongside reduced glare compared with the PL lamp fittings it is designed to replace. Good thermal management supports the stated operating life and lumen maintenance of the fitting over time. This combination of thermal control and glare reduction is presented as a core benefit of upgrading from older lamp-based downlights.

Q: How does Carina compare to Neptune for PL lamp replacement work?
A: Carina and Neptune are both designed to replace older PL lamp downlights, but Carina is rated IP20 and focuses on dimming and emergency lighting options across its four sizes, while Neptune is rated IP65 and offers a choice of four magnetic reflector finishes. Carina is generally the better fit where lighting control or emergency provision is the priority, while Neptune suits areas needing moisture resistance or a specific decorative reflector finish. Both are supplied with a 5 year warranty.

name: Centorio
faq:
Q: Is Centorio suitable for circadian or human-centric lighting schemes?
A: Yes, Centorio's tunable white range from 3000K to 5000K makes it a practical choice for circadian or human-centric lighting, where colour temperature is shifted through the day to support occupant wellbeing. Control is via a standard on/off wall switch or remote, with no app required, so this can be achieved without adding smart building infrastructure. This makes it a straightforward way to bring human-centric lighting into a project without a complex specification.

Q: How is colour temperature adjusted on Centorio?
A: Centorio's colour temperature can be switched between 3000K, 4000K, and 5000K using a wall switch, which also allows dimming down to a night mode setting. A remote control is also available to smoothly dim and change colour temperature across the same 3000K to 5000K range. This gives on-site flexibility to adjust the light output and colour after installation rather than fixing it at order stage.

Q: What bezel options come standard with Centorio?
A: Centorio is supplied with three bezels as standard, in white, satin nickel, or polished chrome finishes. This allows the fitting to be matched to different interior finishes without needing to source a separate accessory bezel. It gives some design flexibility while keeping the underlying fire rated, IP65 downlight the same across a project.

Q: How consistent is the light colour across multiple Centorio units?
A: Centorio uses Epistar LEDs with a Macadam ellipse tolerance of 4 steps or less, meaning colour consistency between individual units is tightly controlled. This matters when specifying multiple downlights across an open-plan space, where any visible variation in white point between fittings would be noticeable. It gives specifiers a technical basis for expecting a uniform result across a full installation.

Q: Is Centorio suitable for a fire-rated bathroom ceiling?
A: Centorio combines fire rated performance with an IP65 front, so it is designed to work in ceilings that need both fire integrity and moisture resistance, such as bathrooms in multi-occupancy buildings. Its tunable warm to cool white output and choice of white, satin nickel, or polished chrome bezels allow it to suit the finish of the room as well as its compliance requirements.

name: Protium
faq:
Q: What is a gimbal downlight and why choose Protium?
A: Protium is a recessed gimbal downlight, meaning the light head can be tilted and rotated within the fitting to direct the beam where needed, rather than being fixed straight down. This adjustable light distribution makes it useful for highlighting specific areas, artwork, or display features within a recessed ceiling format. It features an integral LED light engine and remote driver, designed for easy installation.

Q: What head configurations does Protium offer?
A: Protium is available with a single, double, or triple head configuration, with wattages of 22W, 44W, and 66W respectively, delivering 2310, 4620, and 6930 lumens. This allows one gimbal downlight family to scale from single-point accent lighting up to larger multi-head fittings covering wider areas. All configurations share the same adjustable light distribution feature.

Q: What installation and adjustment benefits does Protium offer?
A: Protium features an integral LED light engine paired with a remote driver, designed for easy installation, and each head rotates through 355 degrees with roughly 30 degrees of tilt. This separation of light engine and driver can simplify fitting in ceiling voids with limited space, while the wide adjustment range allows final beam direction to be set after the fitting is installed. It suits accent lighting tasks where the exact target position is confirmed on site.

Q: What environments is Protium suitable for?
A: Protium is rated IP20 and IK05 for interior use, with an ambient operating range of minus 20 to plus 45 degrees Celsius, narrowing to 0 to 40 degrees Celsius when specified with the emergency option. This makes it suited to standard interior commercial spaces rather than bathrooms, exteriors or areas with a higher risk of impact. Checking the ambient range against the space is worth doing early, particularly where emergency lighting is also being specified.

Q: When would I choose Protium over Protium Max?
A: Protium suits accent lighting tasks needing single, double, or triple head configurations at 22W, 44W, or 66W, making it a good fit for standard retail displays, artwork, or feature walls. Protium Max offers the same adjustable gimbal concept and easy installation but scales up to 25W to 120W across the same three head formats for bigger spaces or higher ceilings. Choosing between them comes down to the scale of the space and the light output needed rather than a difference in how the fitting works.

name: Protium Max
faq:
Q: How does Protium Max differ from the standard Protium?
A: Protium Max is an extra large version of the recessed gimbal downlight, aimed at applications needing higher output or larger scale directional lighting than the standard Protium range. Like Protium, it features adjustable light distribution and an integral LED light engine with a remote driver for easy installation. It is available in three head sizes, each offered in two output levels, giving a wider spread of wattage options than the standard range.

Q: What wattage options does Protium Max offer?
A: Protium Max is available with a single head at 25W or 40W, a double head at 50W or 80W, and a triple head at 75W or 120W, giving specifiers a broad range within one extra large gimbal downlight family. Two colour temperature options, 3000K or 4000K, are available across all sizes. This range allows the fitting to be scaled to higher light level requirements than the standard Protium series.

Q: What installation features does Protium Max share with Protium?
A: Protium Max uses the same integral LED light engine and remote driver arrangement as Protium, designed for easy installation despite the larger physical size of the fitting. This means installation practices familiar from the standard Protium range carry over to the extra large version. Adjustable gimbal heads allow the beam direction to be set on site after fitting.

Q: Can Protium Max be dimmed or specified for emergency circuits?
A: Protium Max supports dimmable options, including mains, DALI, 0-10V, or DSI dimming, along with an emergency lighting version, matching the control flexibility of the standard Protium range. This allows the extra large gimbal downlight to be specified consistently alongside smaller Protium fittings on the same project. Options are selected per head configuration and wattage at order stage.

Q: When should I specify Protium Max instead of the standard Protium?
A: Protium Max is built for applications needing more light output or a larger physical scale than the standard Protium range, while keeping the same adjustable gimbal concept and easy installation using an integral LED light engine and remote driver. It suits larger commercial spaces, higher ceilings, or feature areas where standard Protium's 22W to 66W range is not sufficient, since Protium Max scales from 25W up to 120W. The choice between the two comes down to the scale of the space rather than a difference in functionality.

name: Modus
faq:
Q: What is the Modus downlight and how can it be mounted?
A: Modus is a circular downlight that can be specified as surface mounted or, using the optional 1.5m pendant kit, suspended as a pendant fitting. This gives specifiers flexibility to use the same product in flush ceiling applications or dropped from a higher ceiling where a pendant look is preferred. It has a white or black aluminium body as standard, or custom RAL colour options also available.

Q: What is Modus's diffuser and why does it matter?
A: Modus uses a glass diffuser with a TP(a) rating, a fire performance classification relevant to specifiers checking ceiling and diffuser material compliance on a project. Combined with its IP65 rating, this makes Modus suitable for areas needing both moisture resistance and a compliant diffuser material. The glass construction also gives a different visual quality compared with plastic diffusers.

Q: What wattage and colour temperature options does Modus offer?
A: Modus is available in two wattage options, 14W or 28W, and in 3000K or 4000K colour temperatures, giving flexibility to match different areas of a scheme. It is finished in white, black, or a custom RAL colour to order. Optional DALI dimming is available for projects requiring lighting control integration.

Q: Is Modus suitable for damp or wet areas?
A: Modus carries an IP65 rating, giving it protection against dust and water jets, which suits bathrooms, kitchens, and other areas where moisture resistance is required. Its high efficacy of around 110 lm/W and CRI above 90 Ra mean it also performs well as general lighting in these spaces. Note that the DALI dimming and emergency versions are non-IP rated, so the full IP65 protection applies to the standard fixed-output fitting.

Q: How does Modus compare to Modus Max?
A: Modus is a smaller-scale downlight offered in 14W or 28W, suited to surface mounted or pendant installations in standard rooms. Modus Max shares the same white aluminium body and glass TP(a) diffuser concept but scales up to 70W, 100W, or 150W and is designed to be suspended by chain or rod in larger spaces. Specifiers needing higher output for larger areas should look to Modus Max, while Modus suits more typical room-scale applications.

name: Saturn
faq:
Q: What spaces is Saturn best suited to?
A: Saturn is designed for multi-directional wallwash and accent lighting, with 340 degrees of rotation and tilt from minus 18 to plus 45 degrees, making it well suited to retail, office and healthcare interiors where light needs to be aimed at a wall, display or feature rather than spread evenly across a room. It has been installed in settings including Radley Bag Store at Bicester Village, GovData Offices, and Little Hulton Medical Centre, showing it working across retail, commercial and healthcare environments. This range of real applications gives specifiers confidence it performs consistently outside a single sector.

Q: How much adjustment does Saturn's head allow?
A: Saturn's head can rotate through 340 degrees and tilt from -18 degrees to +45 degrees, giving specifiers a very wide range of aiming positions from a single recessed fitting. This level of adjustment is useful where the exact position of a sign, artwork, or feature is not fixed at the design stage, allowing final aiming on site. It suits applications needing precise, flexible accent lighting rather than fixed downward illumination.

Q: What sizes and wattages does Saturn come in?
A: Saturn is available in three sizes with wattages of 12W, 24W, or 40W, and in 3000K, 4000K, or 5000K colour temperatures. This range allows the fitting to be scaled to different wall heights or feature sizes on the same project. Dimmable and emergency lighting options are also available across the range.

Q: Why choose a Saturn downlight over a standard fixed downlight?
A: Saturn's rotating and tilting head lets it direct light exactly where it's needed, which a standard fixed downlight cannot do, making it better suited to walls, displays and features than flat, general illumination. This is particularly valuable in retail and healthcare settings where lighting is often used to draw attention or support wayfinding rather than simply light a floor area. Specifying Saturn instead of a fixed downlight avoids needing a second, separate accent lighting product in the same scheme.

Q: Has Saturn been used in healthcare settings?
A: Yes, Saturn has been installed at Little Hulton Medical Centre, a project recognised as Healthcare Project of the Year in 2021. This shows the fitting holding up to the scrutiny and performance expectations of a healthcare environment, where lighting quality and reliability are closely assessed. It gives specifiers a strong reference point when considering Saturn for medical centres, clinics or other healthcare interiors.

name: Modus Max
faq:
Q: What is Modus Max designed for?
A: Modus Max is a circular, high output IP65 downlight designed for large areas, available in 70W, 100W, or 150W versions to suit spaces needing significant light output from a single fitting. This makes it suitable for warehouses, large commercial floors, or other high-ceiling spaces where fewer, higher-output fittings are preferred over many smaller downlights. Its IP65 rating and IK09 impact resistance support use in demanding environments.

Q: How can Modus Max be installed in high or open ceilings?

At 7.2kg, this suspended mounting suits industrial or large open-plan commercial spaces. The suspension rod accessory is ordered separately where rod mounting is preferred.

Q: Why choose Modus Max over standard downlights for a large open space?
A: A single Modus Max fitting can deliver up to around 17,000 lumens, which would otherwise need several standard downlights to achieve, reducing both the fitting count and the installation time on large open-plan spaces. Fewer fittings also means less ongoing maintenance across a large ceiling area. This makes it a more efficient specification wherever ceiling height and floor area are both significant.

Q: What control options does Modus Max support?
A: Modus Max offers optional DALI dimming for centralised control of light levels across a large installation. Colour temperature can be specified as 3000K or 4000K, and output ranges from around 7700 lumens at 70W up to around 17,000 lumens at 150W. This makes it straightforward to match light output to the specific area being lit.

Q: How does Modus Max compare to the standard Modus downlight?
A: Modus Max shares the same white aluminium body and glass TP(a) diffuser design as Modus but scales up considerably, offering 70W, 100W, or 150W outputs compared with Modus's 14W or 28W. It is designed to be suspended by chain or rod rather than surface mounted or pendant fitted, making it suited to warehouses and other large, high-ceilinged spaces. Modus is the better choice for standard rooms, while Modus Max fits larger commercial or industrial areas needing more light from fewer fittings.

name: Sounds Like Light - Breve
faq:

The performance comes from its Polyester PET construction, a material chosen for its sound absorbing properties as well as durability. Specifiers can use this NRC figure directly when comparing Breve against other acoustic ceiling products for a wellbeing or acoustic comfort brief.

Q: Where does Breve work best in a building?
A: Breve suits spaces where poor acoustics are as much of a problem as poor lighting, such as open-plan offices, meeting rooms, libraries and co-working spaces, where its 0.91 NRC rating helps reduce reverberation and improve speech clarity while still providing the room's lighting. Because it combines both functions in one fitting, it avoids needing a separate acoustic panel and light fitting taking up ceiling space. This makes it a practical choice anywhere noise and clarity are a known issue, rather than only in spaces where lighting is the sole concern.

Q: Can acoustic lighting be used as a decorative feature rather than just a functional fitting?
A: Yes. Ricoman's Breve acoustic pendant is available in multiple colours for its acoustic body, plus tunable white or RGBW colour change for the light itself, so it can be specified as a coordinated design feature rather than a fixed, off-the-shelf fitting. This suits projects where the ceiling itself is part of the design brief, not just a place to hide services.

A: Breve's rounded rectangle shape makes it a good option where a scheme calls for a softer, more organic acoustic form rather than a sharp edged or capsule shaped fitting. It shares the same Samsung LED light engine, around 120 lm/W efficacy and 0.91 NRC rating as some of the other linear pendants in the range, so shape and colour finish are usually the deciding factors rather than performance.
