A: Yes, its integrated moss panel brings a natural element into the ceiling, supporting wellbeing-focused design alongside its bold triangular form. This makes it a practical way to combine a striking architectural feature with a genuine biophilic benefit in one fitting.

name: Moon
faq:
Q: What is the Moon feature light and how is it typically installed?
A: Moon is a modern architectural pendant with a direct and indirect light output, available as a surface mounted fitting or, with the optional suspension kit, as a pendant. It comes in two sizes, the 875mm SuperMoon and the smaller 585mm MiniMoon, so the same design language can cover both a feature centrepiece and general lighting duties within a building. It has been installed at projects including Windsor House in Harrogate and Burlington Square Apartments in Manchester, showing it working in both commercial and residential settings.

Q: What colour temperature options does Moon offer?
A: Moon is available in 3000K, 4000K or 5000K, with each colour temperature set at the point of order via its own part code rather than switched on site. This still gives specifiers a wide choice of tone, from warm to cool white, to match Moon to the rest of a lighting scheme. Confirming the required colour temperature before ordering, alongside the wattage, ensures the correct part code is quoted first time.

Q: What is the difference between MiniMoon and SuperMoon?
A: MiniMoon is the smaller model at 585mm diameter, available in 38W or 48W and producing from around 4,185 up to 5,295 lumens depending on wattage and colour temperature. SuperMoon is the larger 875mm diameter version, available in 76W or 96W, producing from around 8,365 up to 10,694 lumens. This gives specifiers two size and output options within the same design, so Moon can be scaled to suit a small meeting room or a larger open plan or reception space. Both sizes share the same 120 degree beam angle and colour rendering above 85 Ra.

Q: What dimming and emergency options are available with Moon?
A: Moon can be specified tosupports mains, DALI, 0-10V or DSI dimming, and can also be specified with Casambi wireless control or a PIR sensor. Emergency versions include a standard 3 hour emergency pack and a DALI addressable emergency option, with MiniMoon additionally offering a Z10 remote control integral emergency version. This range of control protocols means Moon can be specified into most standard building lighting control systems rather than requiring a bespoke control solution.

Q: How does Moon manage glare while still producing a strong light output?
A: Moon uses a microprismatic diffuser combined with a direct and indirect light output, so it can deliver a bold visual presence without creating uncomfortable glare for people working nearby or looking up at the fitting. Its UGR rated performance and TP(a) fire classification support specification in offices and other spaces where visual comfort and fire safety are both part of the brief. The same diffuser and glare control benefit apply across both the MiniMoon and SuperMoon sizes.

name: Pulsar (pendant)
faq:
Q: What is the Pulsar pendant and where is it designed to be used?
A: Pulsar is a modern pendant that combines efficacy with elegance, using a minimalistic, contemporary design and durable aluminium construction. It is intended to add a touch of subtle, stylish architectural lighting in both domestic and commercial spaces. This dual suitability makes it a practical choice for design and build firms working across hospitality, retail or residential style commercial fit outs.

Q: Is Pulsar available in mounting formats other than pendant?
A: Yes, the same style of luminaire is also available in surface mounted, recessed and track mounted versions. This means a designer can specify a consistent Pulsar look across a scheme even where ceiling conditions vary, using the pendant version in some areas and the surface, recessed or track mounted version elsewhere. It gives contractors one product family to source and install rather than mixing unrelated ranges to match a single design intent.

Q: What beam angle and finish options does Pulsar offer?
A: Pulsar is available in black or white finish, and offers a choice of 15, 24, 38 (standard) or 55 degree beam angles. This range of beam angles lets a specifier fine tune the light spread for a specific task, such as a narrower beam over a bar counter or a wider spread for general ambient lighting. The finish and beam angle can be combined to suit both the visual style and the functional lighting requirement of the space.

Q: Why choose Pulsar over a larger decorative pendant for accent lighting?
A: Pulsar's minimalistic, contemporary design and compact 10W output mean it can provide precise accent lighting, using its narrower 15 or 24 degree beam angles, without becoming a bulky visual statement in the space. This suits hospitality, retail or residential-style commercial fit-outs where the goal is understated, functional accent lighting rather than a large feature pendant competing for attention. Its consistency with the surface, recessed and track mounted versions of the same design also means the same restrained look can be carried across a mixed scheme.

Q: Can Pulsar be used for both accent lighting and general ambient lighting in the same scheme?
A: Yes, because Pulsar offers a choice of 15, 24, 38 or 55 degree beam angles from the same fitting, a designer can use the narrower angles to pick out a bar counter, artwork or display and the wider 55 degree angle for softer, more general ambient lighting elsewhere in the same space. This means one product range can cover both accent and general lighting roles in a scheme, rather than mixing unrelated fittings to achieve each effect. The minimalistic, contemporary design stays consistent across all beam angle options, so the visual look of the scheme does not change even as the lighting role does.

name: Satellite
faq:
Q: What is the Satellite pendant and where would I use it?
A: Satellite is a modern architectural pendant with a robust cast aluminium body, available in three sizes from 400mm up to 800mm diameter. It can be surface mounted as standard or suspended using an optional suspension kit, so the same design can be specified across a range of ceiling conditions. This makes it a practical choice for offices, reception areas and other commercial interiors where a clean, architectural pendant is needed at different scales across a building.

Q: What colour temperature and wattage flexibility does Satellite offer?
A: Satellite has switchable colour temperature between 3000K and 4000K and switchable wattage within each size, so the installer can set both on site rather than being locked into a single configuration at the point of order. This reduces the risk of specifying the wrong output for a room and allows the light level and colour to be fine tuned once the fitting is in place. It gives contractors one product that can flex to suit a change in brief late in a project.

Q: Is Satellite suitable for spaces with occupancy-based lighting control?
A: Yes, Satellite can be specified with an integral microwave sensor for occupancy detection, alongside mains, DALI or Casambi dimming. This makes it a practical choice for corridors, washrooms or intermittently used areas where lighting should respond to movement rather than stay on constantly, helping reduce running costs without needing a separate control fitting.

Q: Can Satellite be surface mounted and suspended from the same fitting?
A: Yes, Satellite is designed for surface mounting as standard, with suspension available as an option using a 1.5 metre suspension kit accessory. This means the same pendant can be fixed directly to the ceiling in one area and hung as a suspended feature elsewhere in the same scheme, without switching to a different product range. It gives designers and contractors one consistent look to specify across varied ceiling heights and conditions.

Q: What control options does Satellite support?
A: Satellite can be specified with mains dimming, DALI dimming or Casambi wireless control, along with an integral emergency option and a microwave sensor for occupancy detection. This range means the fitting can be integrated into a standard building lighting control system or specified for areas that need automatic switching or emergency lighting compliance. Having these options within one product line simplifies scheduling for contractors working across a mixed use building.

Q: What technical performance and warranty information is available for Satellite?
A: Satellite carries a colour rendering index above 80 Ra, a 90 degree beam angle and an IP20 rating, with an L70 B50 lifetime of 100,000 hours. It is backed by a 5 year warranty, with emergency versions covered for 3 years, and its Class II construction means it does not require a separate earth connection. These figures give specifiers a clear basis for comparing Satellite against other architectural pendants when preparing a technical schedule.

name: Estrella Pro (linear system)
faq:
Q: What is Estrella Pro and where is it typically used?
A: Estrella Pro is a linear lighting system that forms seamless, continuous lines of light rather than a row of separate fittings, giving specifiers a clean architectural look with no visible joins. It is available as a surface mounted or suspended version, so the same design language can be carried across different ceiling types on one project. This makes it suited to commercial interiors such as offices, retail and hospitality spaces that need a continuous run of light, as seen in installations including Sandfield House in Wilmslow.

Q: What optical and diffuser options does Estrella Pro offer?
A: Estrella Pro is available in seven optical variants, including a smooth opal diffuser, a square aperture cell optic, a wallwash version, a microprismatic diffuser and a white louvre grid, so light distribution can be matched to the task without changing product family. Choosing the right optic at specification stage helps control glare and light spread for the specific room function.

Q: Can Estrella Pro be configured into different shapes and lengths?
A: Alongside four standard lengths of 532mm, 1064mm, 1596mm and 2128mm, Estrella Pro can be configured into longer lengths and right angled shapes including L, T and + shapes, letting designers build layouts beyond straight runs. The wallwash version is only available as a straight run, so it is worth checking shape compatibility for the chosen optic early in the specification. This flexibility lets one product range cover both simple corridor runs and more complex feature layouts.

Q: What colour temperature and colour change options are available?
A: Estrella Pro is offered in fixed colour temperatures of 3000K, 4000K and 5000K, plus a tunable white option from 2700K to 6500K, giving specifiers a neutral commercial white to suit most schemes. An RGBW version is also available for colour changing effects, controlled through DMX, radio frequency remotes, Casambi or a wall mounted control, as used at 55 Queen Street Apartments in Manchester. This means one product family can cover both a standard commercial fit-out and a more expressive, colour driven design.

Q: What light quality can specifiers expect from Estrella Pro?
A: Estrella Pro delivers a CRI above 90 Ra across the range with an efficacy of around 100 Lm/W, so colours render accurately under the light while keeping running costs down. Colour consistency between fittings is tightly controlled to within 3 SDCM on the Macadam ellipse scale, which matters when running long, continuous lines of light where any mismatch would be obvious. This combination gives a dependable base spec for commercial interiors where both look and efficiency are being judged.

name: Flow + (curved linear lighting system)
faq:
Q: What is Flow+ and what makes it different from a standard linear fitting?
A: Flow+ is a linear lighting system built from straight, arc and ring shaped modules that combine to create curved lighting features rather than being limited to fixed straight runs. Sections can be joined into rings, waves and interlocking curves, moving the design from a straight line into a genuine three dimensional feature. This makes Flow+ a strong choice for feature lighting in reception areas, stairwells and hospitality spaces where a sculptural ceiling or wall element is wanted.

Q: Can Flow+ be made to a custom length for my project?
A: Yes. While standard lengths and shapes are listed for ordering ease, Flow+ can be produced to any length or shape required, since Ricoman bends and produces it in-house rather than sourcing fixed lengths from a supplier. This means a specifier isn't constrained by a standard part-code list when a space calls for something bespoke. It makes Flow+ a genuine made-to-spec solution rather than a product forced to fit the room.

Q: What makes Flow+'s curves and shapes possible?
A: Flow+ is bent and produced using Ricoman's own bending machine, the only one of its kind for lighting in the UK. This means curves, rings and arcs are formed in-house to the exact geometry a project needs, rather than being limited to a set of pre-moulded shapes. It gives specifiers a level of design freedom that's difficult to get from a standard linear lighting range.

Q: What kind of shapes and layouts can Flow+ create?
A: Flow+ can be formed into straight runs, full rings, arcs from 45 to 180 degrees, and L-shapes at 60, 90 or 120 degrees, and because Ricoman bends it in-house, these aren't the only options available. This gives designers real freedom to create a layout that's unique to the project rather than adapting a design to fit a standard product. It suits feature ceilings and architectural layouts where the lighting is meant to stand out as part of the design itself.

Q: How is a Flow+ installation mounted and put together?
A: Flow+ can be recessed, suspended or surface mounted, with end caps, connection packs, surface mounting kits, suspension kits and recessed clips available to complete the installation. Ring features up to 1200mm diameter include a ceiling rose as standard, while larger rings are supplied divided into arcs with suspensions rather than one fixed rose.

name: Astrowave (flexible 360 degree neon light system)
faq:
Q: What is Astrowave and how is it typically installed?
A: Astrowave is a flexible 360 degree neon light system that forms a continuous 25mm diameter line of light, giving an even glow from every angle rather than a directional beam. It can be installed as a pendant or mounted on walls, ceilings or floors, covering ambient lighting through to accent lighting within the same range. This flexibility allows a single run of Astrowave to become an architectural feature rather than a simple light source.

Q: How durable is Astrowave for demanding installations?
A: Astrowave has an IK08 impact rating and a silicone construction, giving it a level of physical durability that suits busy commercial spaces as well as decorative installations. It's rated to work between minus 20 and 40 degrees Celsius, with an IP65 rating recommended for indoor use, so it holds up in a wide range of ambient conditions. Backed by a 5 year warranty, it gives specifiers a durable option without moving away from a flexible, creative light source.

Q: Can Astrowave be installed as a recessed feature rather than surface mounted or suspended?
A: Yes, when specified Astrowave can be fitted using a plaster-in recessed kit or a standard recessed kit, letting it sit flush within a ceiling or wall rather than being visible as a surface-mounted or suspended run. This gives designers a third option alongside its surface and suspended mounting kits, useful where a flush, minimal look is wanted rather than an exposed light line.

Q: What mounting methods does Astrowave support?
A: Astrowave can be fitted using surface or concealed surface mounting kits, vertical or horizontal suspension kits, some with an acrylic tube, an adjustable solid rod mounting kit, or plaster in recessed and recessed kits for a flush architectural finish. Node plates and single or double node accessories are also available for decorative, multi directional layouts, and a connection kit supports closed shapes such as rings. This range means one product can be specified for a simple wall run, a suspended feature or a fully recessed line without changing product family.

Q: What warranty and lifespan does Astrowave carry?
A: Astrowave carries a 5 year warranty and a life of 36,000 hours, alongside its IP65 rating and CRI above 90 Ra for colour quality.

name: Neon Flex
faq:
Q: What is Neon Flex and what is it used for?
A: Neon Flex is a flexible, sleek 13mm wide light line that flows and bends to create smooth continuous shapes rather than a series of visible individual LEDs. It suits both indoor and outdoor applications, so the same product can be specified across a building's interior and exterior detailing. It has been used in hospitality and residential projects including Hallam Tower Apartments in Sheffield and Studio Powers Architects in Manchester.

Q: Is Neon Flex suitable for outdoor or wet areas?
A: Neon Flex is rated IP66 as standard, covering protection against dust and powerful water jets, which makes it suitable for many outdoor and exterior applications. An IP68 version is available as a special order for installations that need a higher level of water protection, such as areas with prolonged water contact. This gives specifiers a standard option for most outdoor work and a clear upgrade path for wetter or more demanding locations.

Q: What's the maximum length of a single Neon Flex run?
A: Neon Flex can run up to 5 metres from a single point, giving specifiers a practical reference for planning driver placement and joins on longer installations. Runs beyond this length would need to be planned with additional driver points, which is worth factoring in early when laying out a continuous light line across a larger space.

Q: What colour temperature options does Neon Flex offer?
A: Neon Flex is available in 2700K, 3000K or 4000K, giving specifiers a warmer or more neutral white to suit the setting, from a cosy residential feel to a cleaner commercial look. This range means one product can cover different mood requirements across a project without switching to a different light line.

Q: Will Neon Flex look consistent in colour along a long run?
A: Yes, Neon Flex has a Macadam ellipse tolerance of 4 steps or less, meaning colour consistency is tightly controlled along its length and between separate runs. This matters on longer or more visible installations, where any noticeable shift in white point would stand out against a continuous line of light.

name: Aeroline
faq:
Q: What is Aeroline and where is it designed to be used?
A: Aeroline is a series of unobtrusive mini LED light lines with an ultra slim 8mm profile and only 18mm width, designed to sit discreetly within a space rather than draw attention to the fitting itself. It suits under cabinet kitchen lighting, retail, display and refrigeration lighting, where a slim, low profile light source is needed in a confined space. Aeroline has been used in projects including Studio Power Architects in Manchester and a supermarket fit-out in Leicester.

Q: What lengths and outputs does Aeroline come in?
A: Aeroline is available in six standard lengths from 150mm up to 1200mm, each with its own wattage and lumen output, so the fitting can be sized to match a specific run of cabinetry, shelving or a display unit. Output ranges from 210 lumens on the shortest 150mm length to around 1200 lumens on the longest 1200mm length. This lets installers size a run closely to the cabinet or display it is being fitted into, minimising waste.

Q: What connection accessories are available for Aeroline?
A: Aeroline has a wide range of connection accessories, including a middle connector and left, right, T and plus shaped corner connectors, which let runs change direction without needing a separate custom part. Fixing clips are available for both 90 degree and 180 degree installations, along with an extension cable, a hand to hand connector and a 1 to 4 adaptor junction cable for splitting a supply across multiple runs. This range supports installers fitting Aeroline around corners, joints and awkward cabinet layouts.

Q: What control accessories are available for Aeroline?
A: Aeroline can be fitted with a touch switch, a sensor switch or a dimmer switch, giving a simple way to control the light without needing a separate wall mounted control system. A magnet, metal plate and 3M tape mounting option is also available for surfaces where drilling is not practical, and a side power entry point accessory supports different cable routing needs. These options make it straightforward to add local, on demand control to a short run of under cabinet or display lighting.

Q: What colour temperature options does Aeroline offer?
A: Aeroline is available in 3000K or 6000K colour temperatures, giving a choice between a warmer ambient tone and a cooler, more clinical white. This is useful where under cabinet or display lighting needs to match or contrast with the main room scheme, for example a warmer 3000K under a kitchen cabinet against a cooler retail display case. The aluminium body with plastic end caps assists with heat management in the confined spaces the product is designed for.

name: Ricostrip COB
faq:
Q: What is Ricostrip COB and where is it used?
A: Ricostrip COB is a flexible COB LED strip that produces a smooth, dot free line of light rather than individually visible diodes, making it well suited to decorative detailing where the light source itself should not be visible. It is commonly specified for coving, shelving, joinery and display lighting in commercial interiors. Because it is supplied as a continuous flexible strip, it can be cut and routed to follow the exact line needed on site.

Q: What colour temperature and output does Ricostrip COB offer?
A: Ricostrip COB is available in four colour temperatures from 2700K up to 6500K, with a typical output of 9.6W per metre and up to 1000 lumens per metre and 104 lumens per watt at the top end of the range. This gives specifiers a warm to cool white choice from a single, consistent light source technology. A CRI above 90 Ra across the range supports accurate colour rendering for retail and display applications.

Q: What IP ratings are available for Ricostrip COB?
A: Ricostrip COB is available with an IP20 or IP65 option, so the same strip range can be specified for dry indoor joinery or for locations with some exposure to moisture. Confirming which IP rated version is needed for the installation environment is an important step during specification, since accessories such as the electrical connectors are only available for the IP20 version.

Q: Can Ricostrip COB be cut to length on site?
A: Ricostrip COB has a defined cutting unit of 50mm, meaning the strip can be cut at set points along its length to suit the exact run required rather than only being available in fixed lengths. Each run has a maximum length of 5 metres and a minimum bend diameter of 60mm, which is worth checking against tight corners or curves in the design. Ordering the correct metre length in advance still helps minimise on-site cutting and waste.

Q: What's the difference between Ricostrip COB and Ricostrip SMD?
A: The core difference is the LED technology. Ricostrip COB uses chip-on-board LEDs packed closely together to create a continuous, dot-free line of light, while Ricostrip SMD uses individual surface-mount LEDs spaced along the strip at a 6.25mm pitch, giving a more traditional point-source look when viewed closely. Both run at 24V, cut in 50mm units up to a 5 metre maximum length, and carry the same 5 year warranty, so the choice mainly comes down to whether a perfectly smooth glow or a standard LED strip appearance suits the application.

name: Ricostrip SMD
faq:
Q: What is Ricostrip SMD and what versions does it come in?
A: Ricostrip SMD is a flexible LED strip available in standard and high output versions, plus a CTC tuneable white version and an RGBW colour changing version, so one product family can cover a wide range of decorative lighting needs. This gives specifiers a single strip range to choose from whether the project needs a fixed white line, adjustable colour temperature, or a full colour changing effect. All versions are supplied as a continuous flexible strip that can be cut and routed on site.

Q: What is the difference between standard and high output Ricostrip SMD?
A: Standard output Ricostrip SMD runs at around 10.8W per metre with up to 1372 lumens per metre and is only available in IP20, while high output runs at around 13W per metre with up to 1630 lumens per metre and can be specified in IP20 or IP65. This lets specifiers choose extra brightness and a moisture resistant option where the application calls for it, without moving to a different product range. Both versions share the same five colour temperatures from 1900K to 6000K.

Q: What colour temperature options does Ricostrip SMD offer?
A: The standard SMD range covers five fixed colour temperatures from a warm 1900K up to a cool 6000K, giving one of the widest colour ranges in the Ricostrip family. A CTC version is also available offering fully adjustable colour temperature from 2700K to 6500K through a single strip, controlled via DALI, DMX or Casambi. This means a warm fixed white scheme and an adjustable colour temperature installation can both be specified from the same product family.

Q: What does the RGBW version of Ricostrip SMD offer?
A: Ricostrip SMD RGBW combines a 4000K white channel with red, green and blue LEDs on the same strip, giving both a white light source and full colour changing effects from one product. It runs at 17.2W per metre with up to 1150 lumens per metre and can be controlled through DALI, DMX or Casambi. It also supports longer runs of up to 10 metres from a single feed point, compared with 5 metres on the standard and CTC versions, though runs should not be daisy chained beyond the rated driver capacity.

Q: Can Ricostrip SMD be cut to length and how long can a run be?
A: Standard and high output Ricostrip SMD have a 50mm cutting unit and a maximum run length of 5 metres, while the CTC and RGBW versions use a 100mm cutting unit, with CTC also limited to 5 metres and RGBW extending to 10 metres. All versions share a minimum bend diameter of 60mm, which is worth checking against tight corners or curves in the design. Confirming cutting points and maximum run length at specification stage avoids voltage drop issues on longer installations.

Q: What warranty applies across the Ricostrip SMD range?
A: The standard, high output and CTC versions of Ricostrip SMD carry a 5 year warranty and a CRI above 90 Ra, while the RGBW version carries a 3 year warranty and a CRI above 80 Ra, reflecting its different LED technology. This is worth checking against a project's expected colour rendering needs and maintenance plans before finalising which version to specify. All versions are quoted at a 50,000 hour operating life.

name: Luz Macia
faq:
Q: What is Luz Macia and where would it be used?
A: Luz Macia is a plush, microfibre finished LED rope light designed for indoor decorative lighting, giving a soft, tactile line of light rather than a conventional rigid fitting. Its 360 degree beam angle produces an even glow from every angle, making it suited to feature lighting in homes, offices and creative retail spaces. The soft microfibre finish gives it a different aesthetic to a standard rope light or LED strip, which suits interiors where a more decorative, textured light line is wanted.

Q: What colour temperature and dimming control does Luz Macia offer?
A: Luz Macia is fully tunable from 2200K to 6500K, letting a single product move from a warm relaxing tone to a cooler, brighter white. It is supplied with a remote control that adjusts both colour temperature and dimming, so the light level and tone can be set to suit the time of day or occasion without an additional control system. This tunability gives more flexibility than a fixed colour temperature rope light.

Q: How is Luz Macia powered?
A: Luz Macia can be run from either a mains power supply or USB, with a Type C input supporting 5V, 9V, 12V and 20V options depending on the supply used. This gives installers flexibility on projects where running a new mains circuit is not practical, such as retrofit or temporary display work. The included remote control works with either power option, so the same control experience is available regardless of how it is powered.

Q: What are the physical dimensions and finish of Luz Macia?
A: Luz Macia is supplied as a 3 metre length with a 15mm rope diameter, giving a slim profile that can be run along shelving, joinery or display edges. Its microfibre finish gives a soft, plush appearance rather than the harder look of a silicone or PVC rope light. This makes it suited to decorative applications where the light fitting itself is part of the visual design rather than concealed.

Q: Does Luz Macia give off bright, usable light or is it purely decorative?
A: Luz Macia delivers up to 1,120 lumens with a full 360 degree beam angle, meaning it throws light in every direction along its length rather than only glowing softly on one side. This makes it capable of providing genuine ambient light for a room, shelf or display, not just a subtle decorative glow.

name: Luz Agua
faq:
Q: What is Luz Agua and where would it be used?
A: Luz Agua is an outdoor LED rope light with a sleek nylon finish, giving a flexible 3 metre line of light that can decorate gardens, patios, and other exterior or interior spaces. Its 360 degree beam angle produces an even glow from every angle, making it suited to feature lighting around seating areas, planting or building edges. It is built to a durable finish, so it can be specified where a decorative rope light needs to cope with outdoor conditions rather than being confined indoors.

Q: Does Luz Agua give a smooth, glare-free light rather than visible individual LED points?
A: Yes, Luz Agua produces a soft and uniform light output designed to be comfortable to the eyes, rather than showing individual bright spots along its length. Combined with its 360 degree beam angle, this gives an even glow from every angle, which matters for close-up decorative placements where a harsh or dotted light line would be distracting.

Q: What colour temperature and dimming control does Luz Agua offer?
A: Luz Agua is fully tunable from 2200K to 6500K, letting the same product move from a warm relaxing tone to a cooler, brighter white depending on the setting. It is supplied with a remote control that adjusts both colour temperature and dimming, so light level and tone can be set without an additional control system. This tunability suits gardens and patios where lighting needs may change between everyday use and entertaining.

Q: How is Luz Agua powered?
A: Luz Agua can be run from either a mains power supply or USB, with a Type C input supporting 5V, 9V, 12V and 20V options depending on the supply used. This gives installers flexibility on outdoor projects where running a new mains circuit is not always practical. The included remote control works with either power option, so the same control experience is available regardless of how it is powered.

Q: What are the physical dimensions and finish of Luz Agua?
A: Luz Agua is supplied as a 3 metre length with a 15mm rope diameter, wrapped in a sleek nylon finish designed to withstand outdoor conditions while keeping a neat appearance. This slim profile suits use along decking edges, planting borders or patio features without dominating the space. The nylon wrap distinguishes it from Ricoman's indoor Luz Macia, which uses a plush microfibre finish for interior decorative work.

name: Zodiac (48V track system)
faq:
Q: What is the Zodiac 48V Track System and where is it used?
A: Zodiac is Ricoman's range of low voltage tracks and track lights, available in Direct Track, Direct/Indirect Track and Round Track profiles, each backed by a 5 year warranty and offered in 1 metre or 2 metre lengths. Because it covers several track shapes within one 48V system, specifiers can choose the profile that best suits the ceiling and design intent while staying within a single product family. This makes it a flexible base for projects that combine ambient, task and decorative lighting on one system in homes, offices or commercial spaces.

Q: What range of fittings can be run on the Zodiac 48V track?
A: The Zodiac system supports linear lights, recessed aperture downlights, spotlights, decorative rings, globes, flexible neon and pendants, all designed to run on the same low voltage track. This means a specifier can put ambient linear lighting, focused spotlights and decorative pendants on one continuous track rather than combining several separate systems. It reduces the number of different infrastructures a contractor needs to install and wire on a project.

Q: What track shapes and installation accessories are available for Zodiac?
A: Zodiac is offered as Direct, Direct/Indirect and Round track, each available in 1 metre and 2 metre lengths with matching L-connectors and end caps. Accessories include a recessed installation kit for the Direct track, a suspension kit for hanging the track, a mechanical connector plate, and both flexible and straight electrical connectors for building out a layout. This range of fixings supports both simple straight runs and more involved track layouts within a single system.

Q: Why does colour rendering matter across the Zodiac range?
A: Colour rendering above 90 Ra is standard across the Zodiac spotlights, linear fittings, pendants and decorative products, which matters wherever the lit object needs to be seen in its true colours, such as retail displays or feature walls. This means specifiers do not need to check colour rendering fitting by fitting when combining different Zodiac products on one track. It supports consistent colour quality across an entire low voltage installation rather than just individual fittings.

Q: Does the Zodiac system offer anything beyond lighting that should be factored into a spec?
A: Yes, the Zodiac range includes a Bluetooth speaker module, available as master or slave units, with a working range of around 10 metres without obstacles and a transmission power of around 12dB, that runs directly on the same track as the lighting. This suits commercial and hospitality environments where background music alongside the lighting is useful, without running a separate speaker system. Specifiers combining lighting and audio on one project may be able to consolidate both into the Zodiac track rather than installing a separate sound system.

name: Core Plus (backlit panel light)
faq:
Q: What is Core Plus and where is it typically used?
A: Core Plus is a backlit LED panel with a slim aluminium body and an opal diffuser, spreading light evenly rather than showing visible LED points. This makes it a practical choice for general office areas, circulation spaces and feature lighting where even coverage matters more than a directional beam. It carries an IP40 rating for standard indoor use and is supplied with a five year warranty as standard.

Q: What wattage and lumen output options does Core Plus offer?
A: Core Plus is available in 24W (2,532 lumens), 32W (3,362 lumens) and 45W (4,750 lumens) versions, all supplied at 4000K. This range lets one product family cover smaller rooms and larger open areas without changing to a different panel. Choosing the wattage that matches the room size helps avoid over-lighting or under-lighting a space.

Q: Can Core Plus be dimmed or connected to a building control system?
A: Yes, when specified a Core Plus can support mains dimming, DALI, 0-10V and DSI control, and can also be specified with PIR or Casambi options. This means the panel can be wired into an existing building control system without needing a different luminaire for controlled areas. Selecting the dimming option at order stage avoids compatibility issues on site.

Q: Does Core Plus support self-test emergency lighting?
A: Yes, alongside a standard emergency pack, Core Plus can be specified with a Z10 remote control emergency kit supporting manual or automatic self-test. This helps facilities teams verify emergency lighting compliance without manually testing each panel individually.

Q: What light quality can be expected from a Core Plus installation?
A: Core Plus offers a CRI above 80, a 110 degree beam angle and colour consistency rated at SDCM 6 or better, giving a reasonably even and reliable white light output across a batch of panels. The opal diffuser and backlit design spread the light evenly rather than creating hot spots, which suits general and circulation areas where visual comfort matters. This has made it a suitable choice on projects such as the Hallam Tower Luxury Apartments in Sheffield.

name: Core UGR (low UGR backlit panel)
faq:
Q: What is Core UGR and how does it differ from a standard panel light?
A: Core UGR is a backlit, flicker-free LED panel built around an opal, TP(a) rated diffuser designed to reduce glare from the ceiling, reflected in its name referencing Unified Glare Rating. This makes it a suitable choice for desk-based and screen-based work areas, including classrooms and offices, where visual comfort is a priority. It is offered in three sizes so it can be matched to different ceiling grids on the same project.

Q: What sizes and ceiling types does Core UGR support?
A: Core UGR is available in 600x600mm, 1200x300mm and 1200x600mm formats, covering the common grid sizes used on commercial ceilings. It can be installed into lay-in exposed T ceilings, surface mounted, suspended, or fitted into Burgess and metal pan ceilings, so one product range can be specified across several ceiling constructions on the same job. This reduces the number of separate panel products a contractor needs to source.

Q: What does the TP(a) rated diffuser mean for specification?
A: The Core UGR diffuser is a polycarbonate component carrying a TP(a) fire classification, a rating for plastics used in ceiling void applications that specifiers and building control often check on commercial projects. Specifying a panel with this rating built in removes the need to separately source or verify a compliant diffuser. It is a useful reference point when compiling fire safety documentation for a scheme.

Q: Has Core UGR been used in education sector projects?
A: Yes, Core UGR has been installed at Lynch Hill Academy in Slough, Willow Wood Primary School, and Elements Primary School, showing it performing across multiple education settings where low glare matters for classroom comfort and screen-based work.

Q: What light quality does Core UGR provide?
A: Core UGR offers a CRI above 83 and a 110 degree beam angle, giving an even spread of light suited to open-plan offices, classrooms and similar spaces. Colour consistency is rated at SDCM 6 or better, which helps keep appearance uniform across multiple panels in the same ceiling. Combined with its low glare diffuser, this makes it a suitable specification for areas with sustained screen or desk-based work, and it has been used on education projects including Lynch Hill Academy and Elements Primary School.

name: Aquavance (IP66 rated panel)
faq:
Q: What is Aquavance and where should it be specified?
A: Aquavance is an IP66 rated, flicker-free LED panel designed for environments where moisture, washdown or high humidity would rule out a standard panel light. It is suited to medical applications and high humidity areas, making it a fit for clinical and healthcare settings as well as similarly demanding spaces. It is available across different sizes and wattages, giving flexibility for a range of areas and uses.

Q: What does the IP66 rating mean for durability?
A: An IP66 rating on the front of the panel means Aquavance is built to resist dust ingress and powerful water jets, backed by an IK08 impact rating for resistance to knocks. This is why it is positioned for washdown or high humidity settings rather than a standard office ceiling, lowering the risk of luminaire failure in spaces that are cleaned frequently or exposed to steam and condensation. It gives specifiers a starting point for sealed luminaire requirements on healthcare or similarly demanding projects.

Q: What warranty and lifetime rating does Aquavance carry?
A: Aquavance is supplied with a five year warranty and carries an L70 B50 rating of 100,000 hours, ahead of the 50,000 to 70,000 hour ratings seen elsewhere in Ricoman's panel range. This longer rated lifetime is a useful factor for healthcare and high humidity projects, where accessing sealed ceiling voids to replace a failed luminaire can be disruptive. It supports whole-life cost planning alongside the sealed IP66 build.

Q: How consistent is the colour output across Aquavance panels?
A: Aquavance offers a CRI above 85 and colour consistency rated at SDCM 3 or better, a tighter tolerance than most other panels in Ricoman's recessed modular range. This matters in clinical environments, where consistent, accurate colour rendering across multiple panels supports both visual comfort and clinical observation. It gives specifiers a stronger basis for colour matching across a large installation such as a hospital or medical centre.

Q: Has Aquavance been used on healthcare or care sector projects?
A: Yes, Aquavance IP66 panels have been installed in medical centre settings and care home kitchens in the UK, alongside use at Rise School in Feltham. These reference projects give specifiers real-world examples of the panel being used in exactly the type of high humidity, hygiene-sensitive environment it is designed for. This is a useful proof point when comparing sealed panel options for a healthcare or care sector fit-out.

name: Pure Panel (5x5 panel light)
faq:
Q: What is Pure Panel and what applications suit it best?
A: Pure Panel is an LED panel light designed for general commercial applications, making it a straightforward option for offices, retail and similar spaces needing reliable, even illumination. It is offered in a 5x5 format with an IP44 rating, giving it a level of protection suited to standard commercial ceiling environments. Dimming and emergency options are both available, giving flexibility to adapt it to different project requirements.

Q: What size is Pure Panel and what are its core specifications?
A: Pure Panel measures 500x500mm (495x495mm actual, 12.5mm deep) and is supplied as a 30W fixture at 4000K, producing 3,152 lumens. It has a CRI above 85 and a 120 degree beam angle, giving good colour accuracy and a reasonably wide, even spread of light for a general commercial panel. Its slim 12.5mm depth also suits ceiling voids with limited space.

Q: How impact resistant is Pure Panel?
A: Pure Panel carries an IK08 impact rating, giving it a reasonable level of protection in areas with a higher risk of accidental knocks, such as busy circulation routes or communal areas, without needing a specialist impact-rated fitting.

Q: Does Pure Panel offer an emergency lighting option?
A: Yes, emergency options are available on the Pure Panel range, useful where a project wants the same panel to provide escape lighting in corridors or general areas rather than fitting a separate emergency luminaire. This keeps the appearance of emergency and general lighting consistent using one panel family. Specifiers should confirm the exact emergency option needed for each area at order stage.

Q: Why might a specifier choose Pure Panel over a panel with more wattage or colour temperature options?
A: Pure Panel is offered as a single 30W, 4000K specification rather than a range of wattages and colour temperatures. It suits general commercial projects where a straightforward, reliable panel is more useful than extensive customisation.

name: Libra
faq:
Q: What is Libra and what makes its design different?
A: Libra is a low glare panel light that combines a sleek, contemporary design with switchable wattage and colour temperature, letting one luminaire cover several output requirements. This reduces the number of separate products a specifier needs to hold for different rooms. It suits projects where both visual comfort and appearance matter alongside performance.

Q: What does switchable wattage and colour temperature mean for Libra?
A: Libra can be switched between 24W and 36W outputs, and between 3000K, 4000K and 5700K colour temperatures, all from the same fitting. This lets an installer select the exact output and colour needed for a specific room on site, rather than the specifier having to order multiple fixed-spec panels in advance. At 36W, output ranges from around 3,700 to 3,900 lumens depending on the colour temperature chosen.

Q: What control options are available with Libra?
A: Libra supports mains dimming, DALI, 0-10V and DSI dimming, plus PIR sensing, Casambi wireless control, HubSense and Lutron compatibility. This covers both wired lighting control protocols and wireless control, so Libra can be specified into projects with different control infrastructure, including schemes wanting app-based or Bluetooth control without extensive rewiring.

Q: What size is Libra and how deep is the fitting?
A: Libra is built to a 600x600mm format (595x595mm actual) with a 47mm depth, deeper than some of Ricoman's other panels in the range. This is worth checking against the available ceiling void on a project, particularly where a shallower panel has previously been specified. It still fits the standard ceiling grid used across most commercial suspended ceilings.

Q: What environment is Libra suited to and how long is it rated to last?
A: Libra carries an IP20 rating, meaning it is intended for dry, indoor commercial environments rather than areas with moisture or washdown requirements. It is rated for 50,000 operating hours, giving specifiers a lifetime figure to use in maintenance and replacement planning for offices and similar interiors.

name: CTC Panel
faq:
Q: What is the CTC panel and what does tunable white mean for specifiers?
A: CTC is a tunable white LED panel adjustable across a wide colour temperature range of roughly 2700K to 6500K, letting one luminaire move from warm to cool white light to support circadian lighting schemes. This means a specifier can use the same panel to suit different times of day or different room moods without installing separate fixed colour temperature products. Control is available via a wall mounted unit or a remote control as standard.

Q: Is the CTC panel suitable for circadian or human-centric lighting?
A: Yes, CTC is designed with circadian lighting in mind, offering tunable white from 2700K to 6500K so the colour temperature can shift through the day to support occupant wellbeing, controlled via a wall switch or remote.

Q: How is the CTC panel installed and what mounting options are available?
A: CTC uses a back channel design that allows for a number of installation methods, helping maximise mounting versatility across ceiling types. It is supported by accessories including a suspension kit, Z-clips for plasterboard ceilings, a Y suspension kit, offset brackets, linear clips, Burgess clips and metal pan ceiling brackets, so the same panel can be adapted to suspended, surface or plasterboard ceiling installations without changing product.

Q: What control methods does the CTC panel support?
A: CTC can be controlled via a wall mounted control unit or a remote control as standard, with additional DMX and Casambi options available for more advanced tunable white schemes. This range suits both simple installations and more sophisticated colour-tuning setups where lighting needs to change through the day.

Q: How slim is the CTC panel and does it suit shallow ceiling voids?
A: CTC has a 12.5mm depth in its 595x595mm (600x600mm nominal) format, making it a slim option where the ceiling void above a suspended ceiling is limited. This is a useful practical check for retrofit projects where the void depth is fixed and cannot be altered to fit a deeper luminaire.

name: RGBw
faq:
Q: What is the RGBW panel and what is it used for?
A: RGBW is a colour changing, dimmable LED panel designed for creating a unique atmosphere, making it suited to feature areas, hospitality spaces or any interior where mood lighting is wanted alongside general illumination. It is built in a 600x600mm format (595x595mm actual, 11.9mm deep), the same footprint as several other panels in the range.

Q: How is the RGBW panel powered, and does that affect installation?
A: GBW runs on a 24V DC supply rather than standard mains voltage, which means it needs a remote driver to step down the supply. This is worth factoring into containment and driver placement planning at first fix stage, since it differs from a standard mains-fed panel.

Q: What size is the RGBW panel available in?
A: RGBW is available as a 600x600mm dimmable LED panel, matching the standard ceiling grid size used across much of Ricoman's recessed modular range. This makes it straightforward to mix RGBW feature panels with standard white panels on the same ceiling grid within a single project.

Q: What warranty applies to the RGBW panel?
A: RGBW is supplied with a five year warranty and rated for 50,000 operating hours, consistent with the warranty offered across Ricoman's recessed modular panel range. This gives specifiers a like-for-like comparison point when choosing between RGBW and standard fixed white panels for a scheme.

Q: Can the RGBW panel produce plain white light as well as colour?
A: Yes, the W in RGBW refers to a dedicated white channel alongside the red, green and blue channels, and the panel carries a CRI rating above 80. This means it can be used for functional white lighting as well as colour effects, rather than being limited to colour only, which is useful where a feature area still needs to double as usable working light.

name: Sky Panels
faq:

A: Sky Panels are backlit LED panel lights that use a printed sky effect on the diffuser, creating a natural feature lighting effect and a distinctive atmosphere in any workplace. They are supplied as a single panel or as a set of 4, 6 or 9 panels, allowing the effect to be scaled to the size of the ceiling area. Custom graphics are also available beyond the standard sky design.

Q: What design options are available for Sky Panels beyond the standard sky image?
A: Alongside the standard sky design, Ricoman offers a fully custom graphic option, so a project can commission its own artwork rather than using the printed sky. This gives designers a way to create a themed feature ceiling suited to healthcare waiting areas, hospitality interiors or any workplace wanting a distinctive visual feature. High resolution artwork can be submitted to Ricoman for review before printing.

Q: What sizes and set configurations are Sky Panels available in?
A: Sky Panels are available as a single panel or in sets of 4, 6 or 9 panels in the standard 600x600mm size, with single panels also offered in 1200x300mm and 1200x600mm formats. This lets a designer scale the feature area up or down depending on the size of the ceiling void being treated.

Q: How are Sky Panels controlled and dimmed?
A: Sky Panels support mains dimming, DALI, 0-10V and DSI dimming, plus PIR and Casambi options, so the feature effect can be integrated into a standard lighting control scheme alongside general area lighting. This means the sky or custom graphic effect can be dimmed to suit different times of day or activities in the space.

Q: Has Sky Panels been used in healthcare projects?

name: Fusion II
faq:

It suits offices and commercial interiors where the ceiling design itself is part of the specification, as seen in its use at the Gov Data Offices in the UK.

Q: What wattage and lumen output options does Fusion II offer?
A: Fusion II is available in 24W (3,052 lumens), 36W (4,601 lumens) and 48W (6,094 lumens) versions, all at 4000K. This range lets the same distinctive panel design be specified for smaller rooms or larger open areas simply by choosing a different wattage. Matching the wattage to the room keeps light levels appropriate without over-specifying.

Q: How does Fusion II control glare, and how efficient is it?
A: Fusion II uses microprismatic diffusers across its 36 cells, designed to control glare while carrying a UGR rating for visual comfort in occupied spaces. It also delivers a high efficacy of around 127Lm/W, so the panel produces strong light output while keeping running costs down. This combination suits offices and other spaces where both comfort and energy efficiency are priorities.

Q: What is Fusion II made from and how is it rated for protection?
A: Fusion II has a polycarbonate construction with a TP(a) rated polycarbonate diffuser and is rated IP44, giving it a level of protection suited to general commercial areas with some exposure to dust or moisture. This build differs from the aluminium body used on several other panels in Ricoman's range, reflecting its different diffuser and cell design. It is a practical choice where a distinctive ceiling finish is wanted without moving to a fully sealed luminaire.

Q: Has Fusion II been used in office projects?
A: Yes, Fusion II has been installed at GovData Offices. Its microprismatic cell design performs excellent in a commercial office setting.

name: Duoline
faq:

A: Duoline is a high-performance LED panel that delivers 150 lumens per watt from just 40W, giving strong light output while keeping energy consumption low. This efficiency means fewer panels or lower running wattage can achieve the same light levels as older or less efficient panels, reducing energy costs over the life of an installation. It is a straightforward upgrade option where energy performance is a priority on a project.

A: Duoline produces a 4000K white light with a CRI of 80, giving a comfortable, natural appearance suited to everyday working spaces such as offices and commercial interiors. Colour consistency is rated at 5 SDCM, helping keep appearance uniform where several panels are installed in the same area. This makes it a dependable choice for general commercial lighting schemes.

Q: Why does Duoline have a narrow 80 degree beam angle, and what does that mean for specification?
A: Duoline uses a rectangular louvre diffuser that produces a narrower 80 degree beam angle than a typical flat panel, giving more focused, directional light rather than a broad, diffuse spread. This makes it useful for highlighting specific areas or working zones rather than providing only general ambient light. Specifiers should factor this narrower spread into layout calculations compared with a wide-angle opal panel.

Q: What does Duoline's low UGR rating mean for visual comfort?
A: Duoline carries a UGR rating of 18, placing it among the lower glare figures in Ricoman's panel range and making it suitable for desk-based and screen-based work areas. Reducing glare from the ceiling improves visual comfort for people working under the panel for long periods. This is a useful reference point when specifying lighting for offices or other sustained-occupancy workspaces.

Q: Is Duoline certified for hygiene-critical environments?
A: Yes, Duoline is certified for use in hygiene-critical environments, alongside its standard interior applications, making it suitable for settings such as healthcare or food preparation areas where hygiene compliance is a specification requirement.

name: Beacon
faq:
Q: What is the Beacon bollard and where is it typically used?
A: Beacon is a robust exterior die-cast aluminium LED bollard with a classic look, built for driveways, footpaths and other low-level landscape lighting. Its die-cast construction and glass diffuser give it the strength to sit safely alongside busy pedestrian routes, and Ricoman backs it with a 5 year warranty. This makes it a straightforward specification for path and driveway lighting on commercial and residential schemes.

Q: How well does Beacon handle exposure to rain, dust and knocks?
A: Beacon carries an IP65 rating against dust and moisture ingress along with an IK07 rating for impact resistance, so it holds up to the weather and accidental knocks found along paths and driveways. The die-cast aluminium body and glass diffuser add further physical resilience over time. This combination reduces the likelihood of water damage or cracked housings shortening the bollard's working life.

Q: What colour temperature and head style choices does Beacon offer?
A: Beacon is available in 3000K or 4000K colour temperatures, letting specifiers match the warmth of the light to the rest of a landscape scheme. It also comes with a choice of dome, flat top or louvre effect heads, each giving a slightly different beam character and appearance. This range of options means one bollard family can suit both traditional and more contemporary exterior designs.

Where a below-ground fixing is preferred, the optional Beacon Root Mount Kit can be specified alongside the fitting. At 6.95kg, it is substantial enough to sit securely once installed.

Q: Is Beacon efficient for schemes with long operating hours?
A: Beacon delivers an efficacy of around 30 to 80 lumens per watt at 25W, with a power factor above 0.95, so it stays efficient even when running for long hours each night. Its 50,000 hour operating life reduces how often lamps or fittings need replacing along a lit route. This makes it a practical choice for driveways and footpaths that are lit from dusk to dawn.

name: Flosse
faq:
Q: What is the Flosse wall pack designed for?
A: Flosse is an exterior wall pack with a modern, minimalist design, built for building-mounted security and amenity lighting. It suits many different exterior applications, from car parks and building entrances to general facade lighting, and is backed by a 5 year warranty. This makes it a practical single specification for exterior wall lighting across a project.

A: Flosse is rated IP65 against dust and moisture and IK10 against impact, giving it a high level of protection for wall-mounted positions exposed to weather or accidental knocks. Its cast aluminium body and polycarbonate diffuser are built to hold up over a long service life, supported by an L70 B50 rating of 70,000 hours. This level of protection helps reduce the risk of water ingress or impact damage in exposed exterior locations.

A: Flosse is available in white, black or anthracite finishes, so the fitting can be matched to the colour of the building facade or surrounding ironmongery. This means the same wall pack body can cover general amenity lighting, automatically controlled security lighting, or emergency duty, depending on how it is specified. These details help keep installation time down on wall-mounted exterior lighting projects.

name: Hydra

A: Hydra is a robust and lightweight die-cast aluminium floodlight, suitable for exterior and industrial applications where directional area lighting is needed. It is built to work across different scales of project, from smaller yard or facade lighting up to larger exterior industrial areas. Ricoman backs Hydra with a 5 year warranty, giving specifiers confidence in its outdoor performance.

A: Hydra carries an IP65 rating against dust and moisture ingress along with an IK08 rating for impact resistance, so it holds up to the weather and accidental knocks found in exterior and industrial settings. Its die-cast aluminium body and tempered glass diffuser add further physical resilience over a long service life. This level of protection reduces the risk of water ingress or cracked housings shortening the floodlight's working life.

A: Hydra is available in four power options from 50W to 200W, each with its own housing size and lumen output, giving specifiers a choice depending on the scale of the area being lit. Lumen output ranges from around 5,654 lumens on the 50W version up to around 27,744 lumens on the 200W version. This range allows one product family to cover the needs of different environments, from smaller exterior areas up to larger industrial sites.

Q: How efficient is Hydra to run?
A: Hydra delivers an efficacy of around 120 lumens per watt with a power factor above 0.90, keeping running costs down on exterior schemes that are lit for long hours each night. Its 145 degree beam angle spreads light broadly across the area being illuminated. Combined with a 50,000 hour operating life, this efficiency supports its use on exterior and industrial lighting that runs from dusk to dawn.

A: Hydra is wall mounted with bottom cable entry, which keeps the cable route protected from the weather once installed. Its die-cast aluminium construction keeps weight manageable, from 0.94kg on the 50W version up to 5.50kg on the 200W version, and its integral driver removes the need for a separate remote gear tray. These details help keep installation straightforward across different exterior and industrial mounting positions.

name: Alphard
faq:
Q: What is the Alphard bulkhead and where does it work best?
A: Alphard is a surface mounted architectural halo bulkhead designed for optimal light diffusion, suited to decorative interior and exterior applications such as lobbies, corridors and communal circulation areas. It has already been installed in projects including Lynch Hill Academy in Slough and Altitude Business Park in Cheshire. Its cast aluminium body and halo diffusion give it a more architectural appearance than a standard bulkhead.

Q: How robust is Alphard for busy or exposed locations?
A: Alphard combines an IP65 rating against moisture with an IK10 rating for impact resistance, backed by a cast aluminium body and a TP(a) rated opal polycarbonate diffuser. This level of protection suits stairwells, corridors and exterior circulation areas where knocks are more likely. The TP(a) fire rating on the diffuser adds a further layer of reassurance for specifiers on compliance-sensitive projects.

A: Alphard is available in a round or square profile, so specifiers can choose the shape that best fits the ceiling or wall layout of a space. Black is the standard finish, with white available as a special order option. This gives some flexibility to match Alphard to the existing decor of a building.

A: Alphard supports DALI 2 dimming as well as mains, 0-10V and DSI dimming, so it can be integrated into most standard lighting control systems. Combining these functions into one bulkhead reduces the number of separate fittings needed in a corridor or stairwell.

At 2.50kg, it is light enough for straightforward first fix, and its integral driver removes the need for a separate remote gear tray. These details help keep installation consistent across multiple positions on a project.

name: Iris

A: Iris is a surface mounted luminaire with subtle architectural styling, designed for decorative interior and exterior applications such as apartment corridors and communal circulation spaces. It has been installed at Hallam Tower Apartments in Sheffield, demonstrating its use in residential settings. Both versions run at 4000K, keeping the colour temperature consistent across a project regardless of which wattage is chosen. This makes it easy to match light levels to different sized spaces while keeping a uniform appearance.

name: Nexus

A: Nexus is a surface mounted LED luminaire that is particularly fast and easy to install, making it a practical choice for high humidity areas and general interior lighting. name: Academy

Ricoman backs Academy with a 5 year warranty, giving specifiers confidence for education and healthcare projects.

This combination of efficiency and compliance data supports its use in education and healthcare settings.
